    AI Overview
    A Red Flag Warning is the highest-level alert issued by the National Weather Service for critical fire weather conditions. It indicates that a dangerous combination of high temperatures, very low humidity, and strong, gusty winds is happening or imminent (within 24 hours). These conditions can produce extreme fire behavior, allowing fires to start and spread rapidly. 
    Key Usage Examples & Precautions: 
    • Burn Bans: Avoid all outdoor burning, including campfires, fire pits, and charcoal grills.
    • Machinery Use:
      Avoid mowing dry grass, operating chainsaws, or using welding equipment, as sparks can ignite wildfires.
    • Vehicles: Avoid driving or parking vehicles on dry grass, as exhaust systems can ignite fuel.
    • Fire Prevention: Properly extinguish all smoking materials; do not throw cigarettes out of vehicles.
    • Preparedness: Keep vehicles charged, review evacuation plans, and keep kits handy. 
    Synonyms and Related Terms: 
    • Fire Weather Warning
    • Extreme Fire Danger Alert (Commonly used phrasing)
    • Fire Weather Watch (Issued 24-72 hours in advance when conditions are possible) 
    These warnings are most common in the Western U.S. during dry, windy seasons.

    AI Overview
    A
    Red Flag Warning is a forecast warning issued by the National Weather Service (NWS) to signal high fire danger due to a combination of low humidity, strong winds, and dry vegetation. It indicates that rapid wildfire growth and extreme fire behavior are either occurring or expected within 24 hours. 
    Key Aspects of a Red Flag Warning: 
    • Conditions: Typically issued when relative humidity is 15-25% or lower, combined with winds gusting over 25-35 mph, and very dry "fuels" (vegetation).
    • Action Required: Residents should avoid all outdoor burning, welding, or activities that could create sparks.
    • Purpose: To warn firefighters and the public to be on high alert for wildfire ignition and spread
      .
       
    Red Flag Warning vs. Fire Weather Watch 
    • Red Flag Warning: The threat is imminent, usually occurring or expected within the next 24-48 hours.
    • Fire Weather Watch: A lower alert level indicating critical conditions are possible within the next 12 to 72 hours. 
    When you see a red flag warning, be prepared to act quickly if a fire develops, following instructions from local fire officials.
